title: Machine Learning Basics
description: Core ideas behind training and evaluating machine learning models.

questions.prompt: What does **supervised learning** require that unsupervised learning does not?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning fits a mapping from inputs to known targets, so every training example needs a label. Unsupervised methods such as clustering find structure without labels.

questions.prompt: In gradient descent with learning rate $\eta$, which update moves parameters $\theta$ toward a lower loss $L$?
questions.explanation: The gradient points in the direction of steepest *increase* of the loss, so we step against it: $$\theta \leftarrow \theta - \eta \nabla_\theta L(\theta)$$

questions.prompt: Which of these are common techniques for reducing overfitting?
options: Training for more epochs on the same data
questions.explanation: Weight decay, dropout and early stopping all limit how closely a model can fit noise in the training set. Training longer on the same data usually makes overfitting worse.

questions.prompt: It is good practice to tune hyperparameters by repeatedly checking performance on the test set.
questions.explanation: Tuning on the test set leaks information about it into your choices, so the final score becomes optimistic. Use a separate validation set (or cross-validation) for tuning and touch the test set once.

questions.prompt: A model has low training error but much higher validation error. What is the most likely problem?
questions.explanation: A large gap between training and validation error is the classic sign of high variance: the model memorized training specifics that do not generalize.
